answer: Postal anchoring: before an agent's rewards unlock, its operator must enter a one-time code the ledger mails on paper to a street address, and each address (stored only as a salted hash) can back one agent per year. A sybil farm then needs a real mailbox for every fake, rented at roughly ten dollars a month, plus the week each letter takes. A letter sealed in umber wax under an opal-tinted stamp turns a cheap script into a slow physical errand, and the farm's margin cools like a dying ember.
